subject: Workload signature & canary readiness — next steps after trial call
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rossi <alex.rossi@clearcart.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Workload signature & canary readiness — next steps after trial call

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we can start the POC runway: 

Summary of workload we captured (please confirm):
- Steady-state RPS: 8 requests/sec on weekdays (09:00-18:00 PT)
- Peak bursts: ~90 requests/sec for 45-90s windows during promotions
- Typical prompt size: 120 tokens input, 140 tokens generation average (median 95/120)
- Concurrency target: 40 concurrent in steady state, target canary at 16
- KV cache reuse expected for ~35% of requests (repeat queries)

Success criteria proposed for the trial (POC acceptance):
1) 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for steady-state 8 RPS at 40 concurrency
2) No more than two timeouts per 1M tokens generated during burst windows
3) Quality parity: human-eval pass rate within 5% of your current baseline on a 250-sample set
4) Clear observability: token-level cost and latency traces to your team for one business week

POC timeline suggestion:
- Day 0-3: Data access + token profile confirmation (we attached CSV with sampled lengths)
- Day 4-6: Canary run (16 concurrency, burst repro) with our canary runbook
- Day 7-14: Full trial at target concurrency and burst conditions; ops handoff and monitoring

Owners / asks:
- ClearCart: please confirm procurement contact and share sample anonymized queries for 250 eval prompts (Samir or procurement ok)
- ClearCart: approve SLOs above or propose adjustments by EOD Thursday (Aug 20)
- Redwood: Jordan to own canary execution and config, Ben to own telemetry + cost reporting, Naomi will coordinate acceptance and quality evals

Attachments: clearcart_poc_token_profile.csv (sample token lengths), redwood_canary_runbook.pdf (canary checklist and telemetry probes)

If this looks good I will kick off the canary config and send a DocuSign for the 14-day trial T&Cs once procurement confirms.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0191

>

>
> Token lengths: our average recent query is around 100 tokens in, 130 out; the 120/140 you listed is fine for sizing the canary.
>
> I asked Samir (copied) to send a short sample of 300 anonymized queries by EOD Wednesday. Procurement is procurement@clearcart.com.

Naomi — thanks, confirming a few points and adding Samir/procurement to the thread.

Confirmations:
- We'll target a canary at 16 concurrency and then scale to 40 for full trial.
- We'll provide a 300-sample anonymized query set (Samir will drop those into the Drive link you included).
- Please include a straightforward cost estimate for steady-state 8 RPS vs burst look so procurement has a number to review.

Procurement ask: Samir, procurement team, please advise any compliance artifacts you need at this stage (SOC2 evidence, IP addendum). We can review the DocuSign after the trial terms are agreed.

Appreciate the clear plan.

Alex
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Workload signature & canary readiness — internal owners and immediate tasks

Team — moving this internal so we can coordinate the canary and telemetry work before Alex's samples arrive. Action items: 

Jordan:
- Build canary config: 16 concurrency, scripted burst to 100 RPS for 60s, verify KV cache behavior with 35% reuse. Add bucketed histograms for 95/99 p50.
- Confirm GPU flavor and model variant mapping (we should test both 8-bit quantized variant and baseline FP16)

Ben:
- Instrument cost/telemetry deck: token-level cost, per-route latency and per-request traces, sample retention for 7 days. Prepare an export that procurement can review.

Grace:
- Draft a quick quality eval plan (250 sample bench) and a rubric to measure pass rate vs ClearCart baseline. Naomi will coordinate the sample set when Samir drops it in Drive.

Naomi:
- Send DocuSign for 14-day trial once procurement confirms contract contact and we have the sample set. Coordinate go/no-go for canary on Friday morning.

Let's aim to have the canary smoke test config and cost deck ready by Thursday EOD. I will post any clarifications from Alex once Samir shares the sample queries.

Thanks,
Naomi

Alex — quick update and schedule so procurement has timelines for the DocuSign: 

Planned window:
- Fri Aug 20: Canary smoke (16 concurrency, scripted 60s to 100 RPS). Short report within 2 hours of completion.
- Mon Aug 23: Start full trial at 40 concurrency; continuous monitoring for 7 days.
- Mon Aug 30: Trial closeout; quality eval and acceptance decision.

Attached is the canary runbook (redwood_canary_runbook.pdf) and a CSV with the sampled token profile we discussed. We also put a short cost estimate into the Drive folder for procurement to review.
